ABOUT THIS ATLAS

Know the data behind the map.

The folder contains three November 2025 mission and workshop reports (Word/PDF duplicates), plus a neonatal kidney injury review that supplies no facility inventory. The resource assessment provides structured data for 15 facilities.

Sources

  • Facility Resource Assessment Report — extracted data, PATG workshop, 12–13 November 2025; prepared by Dr Hammad Khan and HF team. “Yes” for phototherapy means some equipment, insufficient capacity.
  • HF Paediatric medical mission report, 8–15 November 2025: tertiary neonatal care at EFSTH; mission paediatric surgery at EFSTH and Bansang. Surgery reflects mission activity only.
  • PATG Neonatal Capacity-Building Workshop report, 12–13 November 2025. Unattributed comments mention CPAP equipment, conflicting with the structured assessment’s all-“No” CPAP column; this map uses the structured table and retains that uncertainty.
  • Maina et al., 2019: public-sector health facility database (CC BY 4.0), accessed through an ArcGIS mirror: 101 Gambian facilities. This historical inventory is not a current operational register. Ahmadiyya location: OpenStreetMap / Mapcarta (ODbL); Njau uses an explicitly approximate locality position.
  • Facility aliases reconciled against the strategic plan hospital names and NHIA hospital network. 2017 hospital renamings; Kanifing/Serekunda alias. Resource data attach to these matched facilities, not to neighbouring RCH centres.
  • National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2021–2025: care-level grouping uses the executive summary (minor centres/clinics → primary; major centres/district hospitals → secondary; general/teaching hospitals → tertiary). Assignments inferred from source facility types require validation; ambiguous facilities remain unclassified.
  • Country outline: Natural Earth / geo-countries. Basemap: © OpenStreetMap contributors.

Two distinct care-level classifications

Neonatal services: November 2025 workshop context, with explicit clarification from Dr Hammad Khan on 5 November 2026: Ahmadiyya is primary; Bansang, Farafenni, Bwiam, Kanifing and Bundung MCH are secondary; EFSTH is tertiary (also documented in the mission report). These classifications are separate from the workshop equipment table. Other facilities remain unclassified for neonatal care; no neonatal level is inferred from equipment or general facility type.

General services: the strategic plan grouping described above. These general-service assignments are retained separately, including the inferred general level for Ahmadiyya, which requires validation. A general tertiary designation does not imply tertiary neonatal capability.

Coverage & interpretation

Missing data means unknown, not absent. Coordinates marked approximate are locality-level placements, not confirmed facility entrances. This is a planning and exploration tool, not a live referral directory.
